body.statement: Fix \(w\ge0\). For every \(2\le p<q\) and every same-transitive-closure pair \((G,G')\) in a common topological order with \(\omega_p(G,G')\le w\), actual-row compatibility is decided by the terminal-copy and affine-support tests in \(O(q^5)\) rational-function field operations, and the regular positive-real covariance fiber is represented exactly as the projection of at most \(2^{q-r}\) systems in \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\). For the four-node fork pair with \(p=2\), these are the eight two-scalar systems and their union has the exact projection characterization in \(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}all\text{-}chamber\text{-}projection}\). These reductions do not decide chamberwise density of the projected union. No sound-and-complete realization-or-separator compiler, bit-operation or coefficient-height bound, or pathwidth-to-\(\omega_p\) guarantee is asserted.
body.justification: After retraction of the unsupported compiler headline, this node records only the proved terminal algorithm and finite covariance-branch representation.
body.gap: No local-to-global projection invariant or certified bit-complexity analysis has been proved.
body.consumer: Bounded-width inputs can be reduced and inspected, but this node does not provide a terminating exact covariance-frontier certificate.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(G,G'\) satisfy the displayed assumptions. The value of \(\omega_p(G,G')\) is not needed for either established reduction. First, \(\mathrm{thm:terminal\text{-}certificate}\) is sound and complete for the actual-row class and gives the stated \(O(q^5)\) rational-function field-operation bound.

Second, fix \(\theta\in\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{branch},p,q}(G,G')\). By \(\mathrm{lem:covariance\text{-}branches}\), every legal positive-real covariance twin chooses the unique factor line at each of the \(r\) sources and one of two factor lines at each of the \(q-r\) nonsources. Thus it determines one of at most
\[
 2^{q-r}
\]
systems in \(\mathfrak B_p(G,G')\). The converse part of that lemma reconstructs a legal twin from every solution of any such system, including all exact-support, retained-edge, mixing, sign, and positive-variance conditions. Quantifying \(\theta\) and projecting away the candidate variables therefore represents the regular covariance fiber exactly as the union of those projected systems.

For \(p=2\) and the fork pair, \(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}eight\text{-}branch\text{-}classification}\) reduces each system to \((s,x)\), and \(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}all\text{-}chamber\text{-}projection}\) proves the exact union identity and the chamberwise density condition that remains to be decided. That theorem also proves that the worked rational family and its local regular neighborhoods do not decide the density alternative. None of the invoked results specifies bag transition rules, bounds elimination fill-in, constructs a dense cover or separator for the projected union, or derives the former bit and coefficient exponents. The conclusions proved above are therefore exactly the two stated reductions; the stronger compiler, complexity, and pathwidth claims are not conclusions of this theorem.
